The exponent α quantifies the rate of this decay, reflecting individual subject variability and task complexity. In practical terms, this operator enables prediction of learning efficiency curves, allowing researchers to estimate the number of required training sessions to achieve a desired response threshold. Critically, the model predicts an asymptotic lower bound on achievable latency, beyond which additional practice yields negligible improvement. This provides a rigorous metric for evaluating learning plateau effects and optimizing training protocols.
